Testimony in Support of LD 389: "Resolve, to Increase Transparency and Evaluate Emergency Response Through a
COVID-19 Review Commission"
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and the distinguished members of the Committee on Health and Human Services, my name is Harris Van Pate, and I serve as policy analyst for Maine Policy Institute. Maine Policy is a free market think tank, a nonpartisan, non-profit organization that advocates for individual liberty and economic freedom in Maine. Thank you for the opportunity to provide testimony supporting LD 389, "Resolve, to Increase Transparency and Evaluate Emergency Response Through a COVID-19 Review Commission."
The COVID-19 pandemic brought unprecedented challenges to Maine, as it did to the rest of the nation and the world. The government's response--through executive orders, emergency proclamations, health mandates, and economic policies--had far-reaching effects on individuals, businesses, and communities. While some policies may have been necessary at the time, we must conduct a thorough, independent review of the state's response to ensure accountability, improve future emergency preparedness, and safeguard the constitutional rights of Maine citizens.
LD 389 would establish the COVID-19 Review Commission, a critical step toward increasing transparency in government decision-making. This commission would examine key aspects of the state's response, including:
 The executive orders issued under the declared COVID-19 emergency;  Government contracts related to the execution of emergency policies;  The data collected by the Department of Health and Human Services and the
Maine CDC, particularly regarding suicide attempts, drug-related hospitalizations, and deaths;  The Maine CDC's response, including testing and contact tracing;  The policies implemented by various state agencies, including the Department of Health and Human Services, the Department of Education, the Department of Defense, Veterans and Emergency Management, and the Department of Economic and Community Development.
Maine Policy Institute firmly believes in limited government, individual liberty, and economic freedom. Throughout the COVID-19 emergency, these principles were often compromised. Small businesses were forced to close while large corporations remained open. Families were subjected to extended school closures, leading to severe learning disruptions and loss. Public health data was often inaccessible or inconsistent, preventing the public from making fully informed decisions about their health and

safety. The sweeping powers of the executive branch went largely unchecked, creating a dangerous precedent for future emergencies.1 Maine is not alone in undertaking such a review. Other states, such as Michigan2, Pennsylvania, and Kentucky, have had significant pushback against emergency powers usage during COVID-19. By establishing a COVID-19 Review Commission, Maine would be taking an essential step toward ensuring our state is better prepared for future public health crises while reinforcing the importance of governmental accountability. LD 389 is not about assigning blame but learning from our past and improving our future response. The commission's findings and recommendations will guide the Maine Legislature in crafting balanced emergency response policies that protect public health without unnecessarily infringing on personal freedoms and economic stability. For these reasons, I strongly urge the committee to support LD 389. Ensuring transparency and accountability in government decision-making is a fundamental responsibility, and this legislation provides the framework to fulfill that duty. Thank you for your time and consideration.
1 https://mainepolicy.org/emergency-powers-2023-edition/ 2 https://www.cnn.com/2020/10/02/politics/michigan-supreme-court-whitmer-covid-emergency/index.html

Arizona: in May 2023, Arizona convened the

State of Maine | 132nd Legislature
Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services Testimony of Northe Saunders on behalf of Maine Families for Vaccines and SAFE
Communities Coalition March 24, 2025
Oppose: LD 389 Resolve, to Increase Transparency and Evaluate Emergency Response Through a COVID-19 Review Commission
Senator lngwersen, Representative Meyer, and Honorable Committee Members, thank you for the opportunity to speak today.
My name is Northe Saunders, and I serve as the Director of Maine Families for Vaccines and
Executive Director of SAFE Communities Coalition. Our work centers on building confidence in vaccines, supporting strong public health infrastructure, and ensuring that Maine families are protected from preventable disease.
Let me start by saying clearly: we support thoughtful evaluations of how public health
systems can improve. We're not afraid of learning from the past. ln fact, continuous improvement is an essential component of effective public health.
But LD 389 is not a meaningful or constructive evaluation. lt's a political stunt.
While this bill sounds like a good idea--after all, who wouldn't want to study our response and be better prepared next time?--the reality is very different. Through my work to
support strong immunization laws nationwide, I've seen commissions like this play out in
other states, including Arizona, New Hampshire, and Louisiana. They were billed as
reviews, but in practice, they became political theater.
ln Arizona, the commission was sponsored by anti-vaccine groups like Children's Health Defense. It gave a platform to QAnon conspiracy theorists who claimed COVID vaccines killed halfa million Americans and that all vaccines cause autism. There were no credible public health experts, and no honest or productive examination of the response--just hours of misinformation that undermined trust in science and health professionals.
We can't afford that in Maine.

We don't need a taxpayer-funded stage for fringe voices who want to re-litigate the pandemic. We need investment in the systems that actually protect people--like
immunization programs, public communication tools, and emergency preparedness.
We already have mechanisms for review. State agencies conduct after-action reports.
Independent researchers publish evaluations. And in 2024, the Congressional Select Subcommittee on the Coronavirus Pandemic concluded its two-year investigation into the COVlD-19 pandemic, reviewing over one million documents and producing a 520 page final
report.
If the Legislature wants to improve transparency or emergency response, there are better ways than launching a 14-point fishing expedition that's ripe for partisan grandstanding.
Maine should not follow the path other states have taken--because we've seen where it leads: divisiveness, distrust, and policy based on politics rather than public health.
We must move fon/vard. We must focus on solutions. And we must reject LD 389.
Thank you.
Northe Saunders Portland Maine Families for Vaccines

LD 389, "Resolve, to Increase Transparency and Evaluate Emergency
Response Through a COVID-19 Review Commission"
Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services
March 24, 2025
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and Distinguished Members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Health and Human Services:
I am Trey Stewart; and I represent Senate District 2, which includes several communities in
Penobscot and Aroostook Counties. I am here today to present LD 389, "Resolve, to Increase
Transparency and Evaluate Emergency Response Through a COVID-19 Review Commission."
Those of you who sat on this panel last session may recall a proposal brought forth by former
Senator Lisa Keim. That bill received unanimous support in both the Senate and House of Representatives prior to it being place on the Special Study Table, where it remained until the
Legislature adjourned.
My attempt at resurrecting this commonsense measure is a good faith effort at ensuring public
health and safety, legislative oversight and involvement and, most of all, transparency. This
measure would establish the COVID-19 Commission to review and study the State's response to COVID-19 and report back to this Committee no later than December 3"` of this year. The review will encompass many different areas including state law, the Governor's proclamations
and executive orders and rules and policies implemented by various agencies, including the
Department of Health and Human Services, the Department of Education, the Department of
Defense, Veterans and Emergency Management, Maine Emergency Management Agency and the Department of Economic and Community Development.
What harm is there in reviewing the State's response to a never-before-seen worldwide pandemic? This universal crisis seemed to come out of nowhere and every day brought new fears and trepidation. Those of you who were serving in the Legislature back then must admit that we, as members, were not involved at all with decision-making on how to proceed and protect Maine citizens.
As time ticks on and we move further and further away from the perils of the 15-month long state of civil emergency that began in 2021, I'm afraid the devastating impacts and lessons will
diminish. We must not forget. We must act now. When will the next pandemic appear? We

need to be prepared. You and I may not be here and we need to protect future generations. Learning from what may have gone wrong and capitalizing on what went right is imperative.
Every citizen was dramatically affected by COVID-19 - sickness, death, school closures,
struggling students, depression, mental health decline, addiction, isolation, business closures,
workforce shortages. No one was spared. To be able to look back and examine the protocols
will not only better prepare the state for the future, but a review will also build confidence and trust in our state government.
Thank you for your time and attention.
